CANVAS (blind test): telemetry recovered from orbital physics

Every field below was found without a decoder: candidate byte readings were tested against sunlight, thermal lag, orbital phase, wall-clock time and the IGRF magnetic field computed from the TLE. Names, units and scales are Claude's reading of that evidence, with the satellite name withheld.

Frame type LASP:len212

2998 frames, 46 passes, 212-byte payload

A 212-byte beacon frame from a cubesat (key LASP:len212). Only a frame sequence counter and an on-board clock were located by the engine, so the rest of the frame is unidentified. The clock is a seconds counter on a J2000-style epoch.

Health. Not enough evidence for battery or thermal health since no such fields were identified. The clock shows no resets in the window, so there is no sign of a reboot. The 9 wraps of the 16-bit counter are consistent with normal wrapping by design.

u2be that increases almost always (frac_up 0.996) and wraps 9 times in 4.6 days, which is typical of a 16-bit sequence number. The rate of 0.0048 per second is the average over the observation gaps, not the true rate. The sun/shadow correlations are weak and not meaningful. [3/3 samples agree]

u4be that rises at exactly 1.0 per second with no resets, so it is a seconds clock. The epoch offset points to J2000. The power_bus hint and narrow band are artifacts of a monotonic counter and should be ignored. [3/3 samples agree]

Frame type LASP:len248

1753 frames, 46 passes, 248-byte payload

A 248-byte housekeeping frame with a header sequence counter, several redundant time/uptime counters, and a large block of power telemetry: many solar-panel or channel currents that drop to near zero in shadow, battery voltage and state-of-charge fields that follow sunlight with a lag, and signed currents. Every frame has an eclipse in the previous 80 minutes, so the lagged correlations reflect real physics.

Health. The field names point to roughly nine sequence-counter wraps in 4.6 days, but a 2-byte sequence number wraps by design, so this is not evidence of reboots. The clocks show no resets. The battery fields follow the sun/shadow cycle normally with a state of charge of 95-100%, so there is no sign of trouble, but 4.6 days is too short to judge ageing.

Frame type LASP:len84

652 frames, 43 passes, 84-byte payload

An 84-byte housekeeping-style beacon with a 16-bit wrapping sequence counter, a 32-bit wall-clock timestamp, and a 24-bit uptime-like counter. Only counters and clocks were located; no sensor channels were identified.

Health. No reboots are seen in the window: the 5 Hz uptime counter never reset and the clock ran monotonically. The sequence counter wrapped 8 times, but that is by design. There are no battery or thermal fields, so there is not enough evidence for any other health assessment.
